name: code-commandments
title: Code Commandments
description: The static code checker judges the codebase, its hooks run inside the journal, and every rule and language is a switch in its settings

curl.hint: curl fetches the checker's release binary into the plugin's own folder

python3.hint: python3, 3.9 or newer, runs the plugin's script for every event the journal hands it

sha256sum.hint: sha256sum or shasum checks the fetched binary against its release's SHA256SUMS

setup.name: Fetch the checker's release binary, checked against its SHA256SUMS
Write the chosen switches into config.json
Check for sins, on demand
setup.run: journal check create "Check for sins" --set command=".journal/plugins/code-commandments/bin/commandments-release judge" --set every=0 --set failure="Code Commandments found {summary}"

folders_judged.title: Folders to check
folders_judged.help: One folder per line, from the project root. Empty, the config keeps the folders it names.

folders_skipped.title: Folders to leave out
folders_skipped.help: One folder per line, never read or reported, such as generated code. This list is what the config leaves out.

judge_parallel.title: Rules judged at once
judge_parallel.help: How many detectors the check runs side by side. More finish sooner but use more cores and memory.

judge_read_at_once.title: Files read at once
judge_read_at_once.help: How many processes read one language's files side by side, each writing a share of the files the cache does not already hold while reading them all, so every tree resolves as in one read. It pays where writing the trees is the cost: Python read a third faster at 3. Where reading is the cost it does not: PHP and Vue/TypeScript read slower at 3. Each extra process uses its own core and memory.

judge_record.title: Keep a record of each check
judge_record.help: Writes one line per check into the plugin's own folder: which checkout, whether a tree was held, what was parsed and how long the rules took. It holds counts and file names, never a line of your code, and is what `commandments why` reads back.

judge_edits.title: Judge live edits
judge_edits.help: On, the files an agent edits are judged as it writes, a few seconds after each edit, and the agent is told what it brought in. Off, no agent's edits are judged as it writes, the main agent's included, and nothing is parsed ahead for them. A check somebody asks for, a hand-in and a merge are judged either way.

judge_workers.title: Judge workers
judge_workers.help: The switch over everything below. Off, a worker triggers nothing of ours at all: no judging of its edits, its hand-in or its merge, and no process started for it. On, the choices below say when a worker is judged.

judge_worker_edits.title: Judge a worker's live edits
judge_worker_edits.help: Only with Judge workers on. On, every worker is judged as it writes. Off, its edits are not judged as it writes.

judge_hand_ins.title: Judge a hand-in
judge_hand_ins.help: Only with Judge workers on. On, a worker's hand-in goes through at once, never held, and the plugin judges the files it changed since its worktree was cut afterwards, with no time limit, then tells that worker each sin it finds, naming the file, the line and the skill. Off, a hand-in is judged only with Judge after a hand-in goes through on.

judge_hand_ins_after.title: Judge after a hand-in goes through
judge_hand_ins_after.help: Only with Judge workers on. The same as Judge a hand-in: on, a worker's hand-in goes through at once, unheld, and the plugin judges the files it changed afterwards with no time limit, then tells that worker each sin it finds, naming the file, the line and the skill. Off, a hand-in is not judged afterwards.

judge_merges.title: Judge what a merge brings in
judge_merges.help: Only with Judge workers on. On, a worker's merge is judged in a run the journal queues the moment it lands, over the commits it brought in, and the main agent is told what came in without having to remember. Off, nothing is judged at a merge and what came in is judged whenever somebody next judges those files.

judge_before_merge.title: Judge a merge once it lands
judge_before_merge.help: Only with Judge workers on. The same as Judge what a merge brings in: a merge is never held on a judging; it lands at once and what it brought in is judged afterwards and told.

judge_edit_window.title: Seconds to gather live edits
judge_edit_window.help: How long one agent's live edits are gathered before they are judged together as a group. An edit alone in that time is judged by itself. Zero judges each edit as it comes; more than 60 counts as 60.

judge_at_once.title: Judging runs at once
judge_at_once.help: How many judging runs the plugin starts may run side by side. Each one the plugin starts goes through the journal's process queue, which holds the next back until fewer than this many run.

cache_hours.title: Hours an unused cache is kept
cache_hours.help: How long anything kept between runs stays once nothing uses it: the parsed trees of every language, what each rule answered per file and mypy's cache. Every use resets the clock, so only what went untouched for the whole time is removed.

workers_cli.title: Helpers may run the commandments CLI
workers_cli.help: On, any helper (a worker, a reviewer, a researcher, the merger) may run the commandments program, `journal sins` and the plugin's other aliases. Off, the skills and reminders a helper reads name no such command; nothing is refused, since no hook waits on the plugin. Their work is still judged when it is handed in and merged, and the main agent is not affected.

sin_bare-scope-escape.title: bare-scope-escape
sin_bare-scope-escape.help: an Eloquent query drops every global scope, including ones added later

sin_dead-config-key.title: dead-config-key
sin_dead-config-key.help: A config key nothing reads — dead surface left behind by a deleted feature, which new code may wrongly adopt

sin_dead-event-wiring.title: dead-event-wiring
sin_dead-event-wiring.help: A listener wired to an event class no live code path can fire (`Event::listen`, or an entry of an event service provider's `$listen`) — a listener chain that dead-ends but reads as live wiring

sin_duplicated-config-default.title: duplicated-config-default
sin_duplicated-config-default.help: A config key whose default is stated TWICE — once in the config file, again as the reader's inline fallback — two sources of truth that drift silently

sin_hard-coded-route-path.title: hard-coded-route-path
sin_hard-coded-route-path.help: A path written out by hand where a named route already declares it

sin_mass-update-at-call-site.title: mass-update-at-call-site
sin_mass-update-at-call-site.help: Bare `$model->update([...])` mass-array update at a call site

sin_model-mutation-at-call-site.title: model-mutation-at-call-site
sin_model-mutation-at-call-site.help: Set-property-then-`save()` at a call site (should be an intention method)

sin_repeated-query-chain.title: repeated-query-chain
sin_repeated-query-chain.help: One Eloquent query chain written alike at three or more sites outside its model

sin_request-accessor-recast.title: request-accessor-recast
sin_request-accessor-recast.help: Casting the Stringable returned by a typed request accessor instead of using its `toString()` method.

sin_constructor-orchestration.title: constructor-orchestration
sin_constructor-orchestration.help: A page object fills a public slot imperatively in the constructor (`$this->x = $this->projector->…()`) where a `#[Computed]` property hook would describe it in place

sin_injected-service-not-hidden.title: injected-service-not-hidden
sin_injected-service-not-hidden.help: A page object injects a service (`#[FromContainer]`, …) into a public property without `#[Hidden]` — it leaks into the generated TypeScript type

sin_manual-output-transform.title: manual-output-transform
sin_manual-output-transform.help: A `Data` computed slot hand-flattens a value object into a wire array, instead of a `#[WithTransformer]` that owns the serialized shape

sin_page-object-missing-typescript.title: page-object-missing-typescript
sin_page-object-missing-typescript.help: A page object travels back in a response but carries no `#[TypeScript]` — the `.vue` page reads it as untyped `any`, so the whole page-prop contract goes unchecked

sin_service-location-in-page-object.title: service-location-in-page-object
sin_service-location-in-page-object.help: A page object reaches into the container with `app()`/`resolve()` instead of injecting the collaborator via `#[FromContainer]`

sin_transformer-without-ts-type.title: transformer-without-ts-type
sin_transformer-without-ts-type.help: On a Data class exported with `#[TypeScript]`, a custom `#[WithTransformer]` changes the wire shape and the generated type still describes the PHP value.

sin_boundary-duplicated-operation.title: boundary-duplicated-operation
sin_boundary-duplicated-operation.help: The same domain operation hand-rolled at two DIFFERENT entry boundaries (a console command and an MCP tool, a controller and a command) — one operation with two implementations that drift

sin_dangling-route-name.title: dangling-route-name
sin_dangling-route-name.help: A `route('x')` lookup naming a route no registration mints — a stringly cross-reference that only fails at runtime, as a 500

sin_duplicate-route.title: duplicate-route
sin_duplicate-route.help: Two route registrations of the same verb bind different URLs to the SAME `[Controller, method]` — two names for one handler (invokable single-action controllers, commonly aliased to several canonical URLs, are exempt)

sin_duplicate-route-action.title: duplicate-route-action
sin_duplicate-route-action.help: Two route actions in different controllers thinly delegate to the SAME operation (`return $this->exporter->export(...)`) — the same entry point twice

sin_route-delegates-to-controller.title: route-delegates-to-controller
sin_route-delegates-to-controller.help: A route action forwards to ANOTHER controller's action (`return $this->otherController->action(...)`) — a redundant entry point onto an operation that already has one

sin_all-nullable-data.title: all-nullable-data
sin_all-nullable-data.help: All-nullable "god" DTO — every field `?T`/defaulted (type doesn't tell the truth)

sin_all-optional-data.title: all-optional-data
sin_all-optional-data.help: Every field of a `Data` object is `T|Optional` — the type promises nothing is ever present; the absence belongs on the CONTAINER field where it's used

sin_data-collection-type.title: data-collection-type
sin_data-collection-type.help: A `Data` property is TYPED as `DataCollection` — it should be `array` (or `Collection`) with `#[DataCollectionOf(X)]`; the `DataCollection` type emits malformed TypeScript and skips element-typed hydration

sin_data-method-hint-collision.title: data-method-hint-collision
sin_data-method-hint-collision.help: `@method` tag that re-declares a real method (names the concrete factory, not the magic `from`/`collect`)

sin_hook-missing-computed.title: hook-missing-computed
sin_hook-missing-computed.help: A get-only property HOOK on a `Data` class lacks `#[Computed]` — Spatie reads the virtual property as a hydration INPUT, expects it in `::from()`, and crashes or silently drops it

sin_manual-hydration-loop.title: manual-hydration-loop
sin_manual-hydration-loop.help: Collections hydrated with `::from()` per item instead of `#[DataCollectionOf]` + `::collect()`

sin_manual-input-cast.title: manual-input-cast
sin_manual-input-cast.help: A `Data` value-object property is hand-built at every construction site, instead of a `#[WithCast]` / `Castable` that owns the hydration once

sin_nested-type-missing-typescript.title: nested-type-missing-typescript
sin_nested-type-missing-typescript.help: A `#[TypeScript]` Data has a property typed as a nested `Data` class that itself lacks `#[TypeScript]` — the transformer emits it as `undefined`, a silent hole in the generated type (a nested enum is fine; the enum collector auto-generates it)

sin_non-final-data.title: non-final-data
sin_non-final-data.help: Data class not `final`, or a promoted property not `readonly` on a Data object others can hold

sin_null-to-optional-map.title: null-to-optional-map
sin_null-to-optional-map.help: A producer hand-maps null→`new Optional` — `$x === null ? new Optional : Foo::from($x)` or `expr() ?? new Optional` — instead of one named factory (Spatie's `optional()` maps null→null, the opposite of what a `T|Optional` slot needs)

sin_nullable-wire-object.title: nullable-wire-object
sin_nullable-wire-object.help: A nested Data or pure enum on a `#[TypeScript]` Data is typed `T | null` — it ships `null` on the wire where `T | Optional` would OMIT it (what the frontend's `x?.` reads for "absent")

sin_prefer-optional-create.title: prefer-optional-create
sin_prefer-optional-create.help: A raw `new Optional` is constructed in a runtime expression where Spatie's built-in `Optional::create()` factory reads clearer

sin_data-to-array-roundtrip.title: data-to-array-roundtrip
sin_data-to-array-roundtrip.help: A `X::from(...)->toArray()` sits in a `::from` slot typed `X` that re-hydrates it — build → array → build

sin_derived-collection-cast.title: derived-collection-cast
sin_derived-collection-cast.help: A `#[DataCollectionOf]` is filled by mapping a factory over inputs at the call site, where a `#[WithCast]` should own the derivation

sin_hand-key-remap.title: hand-key-remap
sin_hand-key-remap.help: A `::from([...])` mechanically renames `$src['snake_key']` → `camelKey` by hand, instead of a class-level `#[MapInputName]`

sin_redundant-enum-unwrap.title: redundant-enum-unwrap
sin_redundant-enum-unwrap.help: An enum is unwrapped to `->value` at a hydration site (`'status' => $order->status->value`) where the property is typed as that enum — Spatie re-casts the scalar straight back to the enum

sin_redundant-native-cast.title: redundant-native-cast
sin_redundant-native-cast.help: An enum / date is constructed at a hydration site (`Enum::from($x)`, `new DateTime($x)`) where the property auto-casts the raw scalar

sin_redundant-nested-from.title: redundant-nested-from
sin_redundant-nested-from.help: A nested `X::from([...])` fills a slot the parent `::from` already auto-hydrates from the array

sin_blank-string-default.title: blank-string-default
sin_blank-string-default.help: A blank string default stands for a missing required value

sin_blank-string-on-the-wire.title: blank-string-on-the-wire
sin_blank-string-on-the-wire.help: A string sent over the wire that the frontend reads as absent when it is blank.

sin_cancelled-coalesce.title: cancelled-coalesce
sin_cancelled-coalesce.help: A fallback compared against the same value it falls back to (`(name ?? '') !== ''`, `(name or "") != ""`): missing and empty end up in one branch without saying so

sin_capability-probe-hub.title: capability-probe-hub
sin_capability-probe-hub.help: Several methods each ask the same field if it has a capability before using it

sin_checked-then-read.title: checked-then-read
sin_checked-then-read.help: One lookup is asked twice: a key is tested (`has(k)`, `isset($a[k])`) and then read with the same key, instead of one read that answers with the absence handled

sin_coalesced-loop-subject.title: coalesced-loop-subject
sin_coalesced-loop-subject.help: The loop header replaces a missing collection with an empty one

sin_conditional-array-spread.title: conditional-array-spread
sin_conditional-array-spread.help: A spread branch supplies an empty collection as a placeholder

sin_csharp-null-forgiven.title: csharp-null-forgiven
sin_csharp-null-forgiven.help: The null-forgiving `!` on a value declared nullable — the compiler told the caller it may be null, and `!` silences it instead of deciding

sin_de-nulled-finder.title: de-nulled-finder
sin_de-nulled-finder.help: Every caller takes a nullable result as present

sin_defended-certain-field.title: defended-certain-field
sin_defended-certain-field.help: An `?.` on a field the class declares as always present — a defence against a case the type says cannot happen, so the code doubts something the design already rules out.

sin_erased-null-object.title: erased-null-object
sin_erased-null-object.help: A blank-rendering Null Object written into a `string` slot — coerced back to `''`

sin_false-for-nothing.title: false-for-nothing
sin_false-for-nothing.help: A return typed `X|false`: `false` stands in for "nothing" or "failed", and every caller must test for it.

sin_falsely-optional-field.title: falsely-optional-field
sin_falsely-optional-field.help: A field declared optional (`x?: T`, `T | null`) that is initialised where it is declared — it is never absent, and every `?.` and `??` downstream defends a case that cannot happen

sin_made-null-then-checked.title: made-null-then-checked
sin_made-null-then-checked.help: A local is made null by a conditional (`c ? x : null`) and then checked against null again later in the same function

sin_manufactured-fake-fill.title: manufactured-fake-fill
sin_manufactured-fake-fill.help: An empty scalar stands in for a missing key a lookup is asked for

sin_masked-invariant.title: masked-invariant
sin_masked-invariant.help: Masking an optional field behind a literal hides a value the design requires

sin_match-default-returns-null.title: match-default-returns-null
sin_match-default-returns-null.help: The default arm silently returns an absent value

sin_nullable-callback.title: nullable-callback
sin_nullable-callback.help: A callback is declared optional, checked for absence, and then invoked

sin_nullable-registry-lookup.title: nullable-registry-lookup
sin_nullable-registry-lookup.help: A keyed store returns absence on a miss

sin_option-as-nullable.title: option-as-nullable
sin_option-as-nullable.help: `Option<T>` used as if it were nullable — `?Option`, `Option | null`, `unwrapOr(null)`

sin_phantom-nullable.title: phantom-nullable
sin_phantom-nullable.help: Every dereference assumes the declared optional value is present

sin_placeholder-filled-data.title: placeholder-filled-data
sin_placeholder-filled-data.help: A blank string fills a required string field in a data type

sin_raw-decoded-array-return.title: raw-decoded-array-return
sin_raw-decoded-array-return.help: A function returns decoded data before checking and giving it a type

sin_constant-argument.title: constant-argument
sin_constant-argument.help: Every caller of one of the project's methods passes the same constant for one parameter, so the parameter is not a choice

sin_flag-argument.title: flag-argument
sin_flag-argument.help: a method whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — or on whether a nullable one was given — two methods sharing one name

sin_member-after-method.title: member-after-method
sin_member-after-method.help: A trait use, constant, property, property hook, or enum case declared below a method — so the reader only meets that state after seeing the behaviour that uses it.

sin_member-out-of-order.title: member-out-of-order
sin_member-out-of-order.help: A declaration in the head of a class that arrives after something belonging below it — a constant under a property, a public field under a private one, a hook above the fields it reads

sin_concrete-cross-module-dependency.title: concrete-cross-module-dependency
sin_concrete-cross-module-dependency.help: A constructor takes another module's concrete service

sin_container-reach.title: container-reach
sin_container-reach.help: `app()`, `resolve()` or a container's `make()` reach inside a container-resolved class

sin_interface-overlap.title: interface-overlap
sin_interface-overlap.help: An interface repeats the signatures of a contract it can reuse.

sin_lone-implementer-interface.title: lone-implementer-interface
sin_lone-implementer-interface.help: An interface has only one local implementation

sin_namespace-cycle.title: namespace-cycle
sin_namespace-cycle.help: Two independent modules import each other

sin_namespace-dependency.title: namespace-dependency
sin_namespace-dependency.help: a declared layer references a layer it may not use (the arrow points back up)

sin_orphaned-binding.title: orphaned-binding
sin_orphaned-binding.help: A container binding whose abstract nothing ever resolves — dead wiring that reads as load-bearing and survives every refactor

sin_undeclared-member.title: undeclared-member
sin_undeclared-member.help: A member access the receiver's declared type neither declares nor inherits

sin_archaeology-comment.title: archaeology-comment
sin_archaeology-comment.help: A comment narrates the history of the code

sin_bloated-docblock.title: bloated-docblock
sin_bloated-docblock.help: A type has several paragraphs of description

sin_ceremony-docblock.title: ceremony-docblock
sin_ceremony-docblock.help: A doc comment repeats the function signature

sin_dangling-doc-reference.title: dangling-doc-reference
sin_dangling-doc-reference.help: A document reference points at a declaration the project does not have

sin_inline-docblock.title: inline-docblock
sin_inline-docblock.help: A docblock whose delimiter shares a line with its text — a one-liner, or a block that opens or closes next to content

sin_negative-space-comment.title: negative-space-comment
sin_negative-space-comment.help: A comment defends the code against an assumption the reader has no reason to make

sin_redundant-arrow-return-type.title: redundant-arrow-return-type
sin_redundant-arrow-return-type.help: An arrow repeats the type already inferred from its expression

sin_restated-comment.title: restated-comment
sin_restated-comment.help: A comment repeats the words of the statement it documents

sin_stacked-docblock.title: stacked-docblock
sin_stacked-docblock.help: Several doc comments describe one declaration

sin_converted-argument.title: converted-argument
sin_converted-argument.help: Most callers convert a value the same way for one parameter

sin_divergent-twin.title: divergent-twin
sin_divergent-twin.help: Two functions share most of their uncommon steps, but one misses a step the other takes

sin_duplicate-function.title: duplicate-function
sin_duplicate-function.help: Two functions repeat the same body

sin_list-mirrors-folder.title: list-mirrors-folder
sin_list-mirrors-folder.help: A hand-written class list repeats every concrete class of one type in its folders

sin_near-duplicate-function.title: near-duplicate-function
sin_near-duplicate-function.help: Two functions run the same code with different names or data

sin_recast-result.title: recast-result
sin_recast-result.help: Most callers convert what one of the project's methods returns the same way, instead of the method returning that type

sin_repeated-folder-path.title: repeated-folder-path
sin_repeated-folder-path.help: One folder is spelled out at three or more sites across separate scopes

sin_repeated-guard.title: repeated-guard
sin_repeated-guard.help: A compound condition about an object is written out at more than one site

sin_repeated-named-call.title: repeated-named-call
sin_repeated-named-call.help: The same `with`-style method is called with the same named argument at 2+ sites, instead of a named helper on the type.

sin_repeated-record-shape.title: repeated-record-shape
sin_repeated-record-shape.help: One call is handed a keyed array of the same keys, with a part of the same values, at more than one site, instead of a named constructor on the type it fills

sin_repeated-static-factory.title: repeated-static-factory
sin_repeated-static-factory.help: One function asks a static factory for the same object twice, with the same arguments, and asks each one something, instead of holding the object and asking it

sin_repeated-type-guard.title: repeated-type-guard
sin_repeated-type-guard.help: The same compound type check is written out at more than one site

sin_unnamed-vocabulary-literal.title: unnamed-vocabulary-literal
sin_unnamed-vocabulary-literal.help: A string literal fills a parameter that already has a named constant for that value

sin_compare-self.title: compare-self
sin_compare-self.help: A strict comparison bypasses an enum's verified comparison method.

sin_const-class-enum.title: const-class-enum
sin_const-class-enum.help: A class of constants defines a closed set of cases

sin_enum-case-or-chain.title: enum-case-or-chain
sin_enum-case-or-chain.help: An or-chain asks about several cases of one enum

sin_enum-value-match.title: enum-value-match
sin_enum-value-match.help: A `match` or `switch` over an enum's backing value at the call site: logic that belongs on the enum but lives elsewhere instead.

sin_in-array-mirrors-enum.title: in-array-mirrors-enum
sin_in-array-mirrors-enum.help: A literal membership check repeats declared enum values

sin_side-table-trait.title: side-table-trait
sin_side-table-trait.help: A separate list repeats which cases have a trait

sin_string-match-mirrors-enum.title: string-match-mirrors-enum
sin_string-match-mirrors-enum.help: A switch repeats literal values already declared as cases

sin_type-switch.title: type-switch
sin_type-switch.help: Dispatch branches test the same value against several concrete types

sin_generic-exception.title: generic-exception
sin_generic-exception.help: A throw of the language's catch-all failure (`Exception`, `RuntimeException`, `Error`, `RuntimeError`) instead of a named one

sin_message-at-throw.title: message-at-throw
sin_message-at-throw.help: A failure's message written as a string at the throw, not by a named constructor given the values involved

sin_rethrown-unchanged.title: rethrown-unchanged
sin_rethrown-unchanged.help: A `catch` whose whole body throws back the failure it caught: it adds nothing, which is what writing no clause does

sin_swallow-catch.title: swallow-catch
sin_swallow-catch.help: A `catch` whose body is empty, or only returns `null`/`false`/an empty value or moves on: the failure becomes something that looks like an answer

sin_wrapping-without-cause.title: wrapping-without-cause
sin_wrapping-without-cause.help: A new failure thrown inside a `catch` without the caught one as its cause: the trace of where it started is lost

sin_constructor-side-effect.title: constructor-side-effect
sin_constructor-side-effect.help: A constructor that performs a side effect on a collaborator and throws away the result, so simply creating the object changes something outside it.

sin_csharp-blocked-await.title: csharp-blocked-await
sin_csharp-blocked-await.help: `.Result`, `.Wait()` or `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` on a task — the thread it blocks is the one the work needed back, so it deadlocks under load and nowhere else

sin_mutable-static-state.title: mutable-static-state
sin_mutable-static-state.help: A write to a static property — really a global variable with a namespace attached — where whichever write happens last wins, so the order code runs in changes the result.

sin_python-blocked-await.title: python-blocked-await
sin_python-blocked-await.help: `time.sleep`, `requests.get` or `subprocess.run` inside an `async def` — the thread it stops is the event loop, so every coroutine waiting on it stops too

sin_python-frozen-default.title: python-frozen-default
sin_python-frozen-default.help: a parameter defaulted to `datetime.now()`, `uuid4()` or another call that answers differently each time — it runs once when the def is defined, so every call that omits it gets the moment the module was imported

sin_python-mutable-default.title: python-mutable-default
sin_python-mutable-default.help: a parameter defaulted to a `[]`, `{}` or `set()` — one container, made once, shared by every call that omits it

sin_unread-collaborator.title: unread-collaborator
sin_unread-collaborator.help: a collaborator promoted into a private field by the constructor and never read anywhere in the class — the class asks for something it does not use, and only a search of the whole type says so

sin_collection-mutated-while-iterated.title: collection-mutated-while-iterated
sin_collection-mutated-while-iterated.help: a `foreach` that adds to or removes from the very collection it walks — the enumerator reads a collection that moved under it, which throws InvalidOperationException

sin_csharp-inline-throw.title: csharp-inline-throw
sin_csharp-inline-throw.help: a `?? throw` inside a call's argument or in front of a member call — the check that stops the method is hidden in the middle of the work

sin_deep-nesting.title: deep-nesting
sin_deep-nesting.help: A decision sits deep inside other decisions in one function

sin_duplicated-branch-tail.title: duplicated-branch-tail
sin_duplicated-branch-tail.help: Every branch of an `if`/`else` ends with the same statement: it runs whichever way the condition goes.

sin_if-else-ladder.title: if-else-ladder
sin_if-else-ladder.help: if/elseif ladder of 4+ branches (should be match/dispatch)

sin_inline-throw.title: inline-throw
sin_inline-throw.help: `?? throw` fed into a call or dereferenced on the same line (inline throw mid-expression)

sin_loop-inverted-guard.title: loop-inverted-guard
sin_loop-inverted-guard.help: A loop whose whole body is one `if` (no `else`) around real work: the iteration pushed a level deep behind a condition

sin_nested-ternary.title: nested-ternary
sin_nested-ternary.help: A conditional expression (`a ? b : c`, `b if a else c`) with another inside it: several decisions folded into one expression

sin_non-counting-for.title: non-counting-for
sin_non-counting-for.help: A `for` loop whose step assigns the next item instead of moving a counter: a walk written as a count

sin_query-in-loop.title: query-in-loop
sin_query-in-loop.help: a query run inside a loop — one query per turn, so the work grows with the data while the code reads as though it were one call

sin_reassigned-parameter.title: reassigned-parameter
sin_reassigned-parameter.help: A parameter overwritten inside its function, so one name holds the value the caller passed and later a different one.

sin_redundant-else.title: redundant-else
sin_redundant-else.help: An `else` after an `if` branch that already left (it returns, throws, breaks or continues): it indents the rest for nothing

sin_short-circuit-statement.title: short-circuit-statement
sin_short-circuit-statement.help: A bare `a && b()` or `a || b()` statement: a short-circuit whose value nothing reads, so the operator is an `if` in disguise

sin_subject-ladder.title: subject-ladder
sin_subject-ladder.help: An `if`/`else if` chain of four or more rungs that each test the same subject for equality with a constant: a dispatch written as a ladder

sin_ternary-statement.title: ternary-statement
sin_ternary-statement.help: A bare conditional expression as a statement (`cond ? doThis() : doThat()`): its value is never read, so it chooses an action, not a value

sin_unnamed-condition.title: unnamed-condition
sin_unnamed-condition.help: A condition of three or more parts over two or more objects whose decision has no name

sin_unreachable-statement.title: unreachable-statement
sin_unreachable-statement.help: A statement after one that never completes (a return, throw, break or continue, an if whose every arm leaves, a loop that never ends): it can never run.

sin_bare-state-predicate.title: bare-state-predicate
sin_bare-state-predicate.help: A `bool` about the object's own state named as a bare verb — `binds()`, `spins()` — where a question belongs

sin_narrated-command.title: narrated-command
sin_narrated-command.help: A command named in the third person — `hides()`, `entersTestMode()` — where a call is an order, not a description of one

sin_computed-boolean-argument.title: computed-boolean-argument
sin_computed-boolean-argument.help: A parameter that's just true/false, computed by every caller from the same object it could be given instead.

sin_derived-argument.title: derived-argument
sin_derived-argument.help: Passing the same object twice, once whole and once broken into a piece, or broken into several pieces at once, when the callee could derive each piece itself from the one object.

sin_param-resolved-from-param.title: param-resolved-from-param
sin_param-resolved-from-param.help: Unpacking the target out of a container parameter: a method takes a container and a key (a workflow and a node id) and resolves the node itself, when it could just receive the node.

sin_hand-rolled-registry.title: hand-rolled-registry
sin_hand-rolled-registry.help: A class writes its own keyed store (fill under a key, throw on a missing key) instead of extending the one Registry base

sin_feature-envy.title: feature-envy
sin_feature-envy.help: Exiled behaviour / feature envy — a method operating on ONE other owned object's internals that belongs ON that object

sin_guard-beside-transition.title: guard-beside-transition
sin_guard-beside-transition.help: A caller checks an object's state against an enum case and throws, then tells that object to change: the rule sits outside the transition it guards

sin_handed-out-collection.title: handed-out-collection
sin_handed-out-collection.help: A getter whose whole body returns the object's own mutable collection, untouched: every caller holds the same one and may add, remove or reorder it behind the object's back.

sin_middle-man.title: middle-man
sin_middle-man.help: A class whose every public method only hands its arguments, unchanged, to the same field: it adds nothing between the caller and the object that does the work.

sin_train-wreck.title: train-wreck
sin_train-wreck.help: A call chain through three of the project's own types (`order.customer().address().city()`), so a change three objects away reaches this caller.

sin_assembled-template.title: assembled-template
sin_assembled-template.help: A multi-line template assembled as an array of line fragments and joined with a newline — the output is unreadable in the source that emits it

sin_filled-parameter.title: filled-parameter
sin_filled-parameter.help: a `void` method that writes a property of an object it was handed, whose caller then reads what it handed over — the signature says the object goes in and nothing says it comes out changed

sin_impossible-guard.title: impossible-guard
sin_impossible-guard.help: `if ($order === null)` where `$order` is typed `Order`, with no `?` — one of the two is wrong, and both are worth knowing

sin_python-constant-property.title: python-constant-property
sin_python-constant-property.help: an `@property` whose body never reads `self` — `return "box"` — a stored value made to look like a computed one.

sin_refused-bequest.title: refused-bequest
sin_refused-bequest.help: A method that overrides or implements an inherited one only to throw: the class claims a contract it refuses to keep.

sin_scratch-state-restore.title: scratch-state-restore
sin_scratch-state-restore.help: Scratch state on the object: a method saves one of its own fields to a local and restores it later, the field really a per-call input.

sin_unused-parameter.title: unused-parameter
sin_unused-parameter.help: A parameter of a method no subclass can override that its body never reads: every caller must pass a value nothing uses.

sin_unused-private-member.title: unused-private-member
sin_unused-private-member.help: A private method nothing in its class calls, or a private property nothing in its class reads: dead code the class still carries.

sin_useless-property-hook.title: useless-property-hook
sin_useless-property-hook.help: A property's getter that reads nothing from the object: a stored property wearing computed syntax.

sin_coupled-fields.title: coupled-fields
sin_coupled-fields.help: A class's own fields always change and get checked together — one concept split across several fields — and should be folded into a single value object.

sin_data-clump.title: data-clump
sin_data-clump.help: The same group of scalar parameters appears on different types

sin_flat-field-cluster.title: flat-field-cluster
sin_flat-field-cluster.help: A `#[TypeScript]` `Data` class spreads a value object it already models flat across sibling scalar fields sharing a camelCase prefix (`wireType` + `wireLabel`) instead of nesting the existing `Wire{type, label}`.

sin_hand-rolled-wither.title: hand-rolled-wither
sin_hand-rolled-wither.help: A wither method rebuilds the whole object by re-listing every constructor field, so adding a new field means updating every wither in the class.

sin_mutable-value-object.title: mutable-value-object
sin_mutable-value-object.help: A value type that mutates its own field after construction, so two things holding what should be the same value can end up different — one changes without the other knowing.

sin_positional-tuple-return.title: positional-tuple-return
sin_positional-tuple-return.help: Returning a positional TUPLE — `return [$node, $key, $inputs, $outputs]` — bundling independent values as a keyless list the caller destructures by position

sin_mirrored-server-type.title: mirrored-server-type
sin_mirrored-server-type.help: A hand-written TypeScript type mirrors a backend `Data` class one-to-one — two sources of truth for one contract that drift the moment the server shape changes

sin_hard-coded-server-url.title: hard-coded-server-url
sin_hard-coded-server-url.help: A string written out as the path of a route the server declares by name

sin_raw-fetch-in-component.title: raw-fetch-in-component
sin_raw-fetch-in-component.help: A Vue component calls the global `fetch` itself instead of the one client module

sin_compound-inline-component.title: compound-inline-component
sin_compound-inline-component.help: A compound primitive (`Dialog`/`Card`/`Sheet`/`Tabs`…) assembled inline with a substantial body — extract it into its own named component.

sin_deep-data-reach.title: deep-data-reach
sin_deep-data-reach.help: A group of elements in a sizeable template that all reach deep into the same nested object (≥2 distinct fields) — extract the shared mid-object into a component that takes it as a prop.

sin_deep-nested.title: deep-nested
sin_deep-nested.help: Template markup nested far too deep — extract a subtree as its own component

sin_duplicate-element.title: duplicate-element
sin_duplicate-element.help: Identical markup (3+ elements) repeated 2+ times — within a template or across components — extract one component

sin_inline-case-views.title: inline-case-views
sin_inline-case-views.help: A dispatch whose cases each render a whole view inline — one component doing a job per case

sin_near-duplicate-element.title: near-duplicate-element
sin_near-duplicate-element.help: Markup with one skeleton repeated 2+ times — the same tags, attributes and nesting binding different data — within a template, across components, or as two components' whole templates

sin_oversized-component.title: oversized-component
sin_oversized-component.help: A component whose template renders more elements than the project's declared budget — one component doing several jobs

sin_prop-drilling.title: prop-drilling
sin_prop-drilling.help: A prop forwarded through a chain of 2+ components, none of which read it — passed down through components that only pass it further.

sin_prop-mutation.title: prop-mutation
sin_prop-mutation.help: A prop is written to — `v-model` bound to it, or `@event="prop = …"` — but props are read-only (a build error or a silent no-op).

sin_control-flow-on-element.title: control-flow-on-element
sin_control-flow-on-element.help: `v-if`/`v-for`/`v-else`/`v-else-if` on an HTML/component tag instead of a `<template>`

sin_index-as-key.title: index-as-key
sin_index-as-key.help: `:key` bound to the `v-for` index — a positional key corrupts state when the list reorders or an item is inserted

sin_loop-with-condition.title: loop-with-condition
sin_loop-with-condition.help: `v-for` and `v-if`/`v-else-if` on the same element — the condition is re-evaluated every iteration.

sin_re-tested-switch-case.title: re-tested-switch-case
sin_re-tested-switch-case.help: A `<SwitchCase>` case that tests again the value the `<SwitchCase>` already dispatched on

sin_switch-case.title: switch-case
sin_switch-case.help: A `v-if`/`v-else-if` chain re-testing the same subject (should be `<SwitchCase :value>`)
